child_drawing_rules_compiled.pdf.note: Self-describes as 'not diagnostic rules; many are speculative or weakly supported' in its own introduction.

entries.original_text: رسم العيون الواسعة يدل على الشخصية المنفتحة.
entries.possible_interpretation: outgoing personality

entries.original_text: رسم العيون الصارمة يدل على الشعور بالغضب.
entries.possible_interpretation: feeling of anger

entries.original_text: رسم العيون المغمضة يدل على رفض الشخص النظر إلى نفسه من الداخل ورفضه الاعتراف بعيوبه.
entries.possible_interpretation: refusal to look inward / acknowledge one's own faults

entries.original_text: رسم النمر أو الذئب يدل على الشعور بالغضب.
entries.possible_interpretation: feeling of anger

entries.original_text: رسم الثعلب يدل على أن الرسام كان يفكر في عمل أمر لئيم أو خبيث.
entries.possible_interpretation: thinking of doing something mean/malicious

entries.original_text: رسم السنجاب يشير إلى حاجة الرسام للحماية والاهتمام.
entries.possible_interpretation: need for protection and attention

entries.original_text: رسم الأسد يشير إلى اعتقاد الشخص بأنه متفوق على الآخرين.
entries.possible_interpretation: belief in one's own superiority

entries.original_text: حب رسم الأشكال الهندسية يشير إلى كثرة الأهداف والخطط والعناد والإصرار.
entries.possible_interpretation: many goals/plans, stubbornness, persistence

entries.original_text: رسم النجوم يشير إلى أن الشخص يريد أن يكون ملفتاً لنظر الجميع.
entries.possible_interpretation: wanting to be the center of attention

entries.original_text: رسم الزهور والسحب والشمس قد يعبر عن تخيل أهداف وأفكار جديدة وشخصية إيجابية ومزاج جيد.
entries.possible_interpretation: imagining new goals/ideas, positive personality, good mood (only if drawn while distracted/absent-minded)

entries.original_text: رسم الدوائر يعبر عن الشعور بالوحدة والحاجة إلى شخص قريب يقف بجانبه.
entries.possible_interpretation: feeling of loneliness, need for someone close

entries.original_text: رسم وسائل النقل يشير إلى حب السفر والعطلة والاجتماعية والانفتاح والمرح والمغامرة وحب الحياة.
entries.possible_interpretation: loves travel/vacations, social, outgoing, playful, adventurous

entries.original_text: رسم القلوب يدل على شخصية عاطفية أو عاشقة واجتماعية ورومانسية لطيفة وقادرة على جذب قلوب الآخرين.
entries.possible_interpretation: affectionate/loving personality, social, romantic, able to attract others

entries.original_text: إذا غطت الرسمة نحو 50% من الورقة فقد تدل على الانفتاح أحياناً والانطواء أحياناً أخرى.
entries.possible_interpretation: outgoing at times, introverted at other times

entries.original_text: إذا غطت الرسمة كل الورقة فهذا يدل على احترام الشخص العالي لنفسه وتقديره لها.
entries.possible_interpretation: high self-respect/self-esteem

entries.original_text: إذا لم تتجاوز الرسمة 20% من الورقة فقد يدل ذلك على عدم الاستقرار أو الخوف.
entries.possible_interpretation: instability or fear

entries.original_text: الرسم في أعلى الصفحة قد يعبر عن شخصية حالمة أو واقع خيالي وصعوبة في التكيف.
entries.possible_interpretation: dreamy personality, fantasy world, difficulty adapting

entries.original_text: الرسم في الجانب الأيسر يدل على شخصية انطوائية.
entries.possible_interpretation: introverted personality

entries.original_text: الرسم في الجانب الأيمن يدل على شخصية منفتحة.
entries.possible_interpretation: outgoing personality

entries.original_text: Single drawing: Can suggest a possibility, but cannot diagnose depression, abuse, anxiety, or personality.
Patterns across drawings: Repeated themes over time are more informative than one picture.
Child's explanation: Always ask what the drawing means to the child.
Age and skill: Development, motor skill, and cultural style can change the drawing a lot.
Wide eyes: Often interpreted as openness or alertness; in some emotion-drawing work, wide eyes can also fit fear/surprise.
entries.possible_interpretation: openness or alertness; sometimes fear/surprise
entries.notes_as_written: Children's facial-expression drawings research; general projective tradition.

entries.original_text: Strict, narrowed, or intense eyes: May be read as anger, tension, suspicion, or defensiveness.
entries.possible_interpretation: anger, tension, suspicion, or defensiveness

entries.original_text: Closed eyes: Sometimes interpreted as avoidance, shutting out the world, or refusing to look inward.
entries.possible_interpretation: avoidance, shutting out the world, or refusing to look inward

entries.original_text: Eyes with little detail or missing eyes: May suggest withdrawal, avoidance, low interest in contact, or simply limited drawing skill.
entries.possible_interpretation: withdrawal, avoidance, low interest in contact, or limited drawing skill
entries.notes_as_written: Projective drawing heuristics; developmental factors important.

entries.original_text: Face expression: Smiling can suggest positive tone; sad, tense, or frightened faces can suggest distress.
entries.possible_interpretation: positive tone (smiling) or distress (sad/tense/frightened)
entries.notes_as_written: Children do encode emotions in faces, but not as a diagnosis test.

entries.original_text: Tiger or wolf: Often informally linked with anger, threat, or aggression.
entries.possible_interpretation: anger, threat, or aggression

entries.original_text: Fox: Sometimes informally linked with sneakiness or cunning.
entries.possible_interpretation: sneakiness or cunning

entries.original_text: Squirrel: Sometimes linked with need for protection, nervous energy, or seeking care.
entries.possible_interpretation: need for protection, nervous energy, or seeking care

entries.original_text: Lion: Sometimes linked with dominance, pride, strength, or superiority.
entries.possible_interpretation: dominance, pride, strength, or superiority

entries.original_text: Animal choice in general: Can reflect interests, story play, fear, identification, or a projective theme.
entries.possible_interpretation: interests, story play, fear, identification, or a projective theme

entries.original_text: Geometric shapes preferred: Sometimes interpreted as planning, control, persistence, or stubbornness.
entries.possible_interpretation: planning, control, persistence, or stubbornness

entries.original_text: Stars: Sometimes read as wanting attention, admiration, or visibility.
entries.possible_interpretation: wanting attention, admiration, or visibility

entries.original_text: Circles: Sometimes associated with unity, wholeness, or the need for closeness; in your handout, loneliness and need for support.
entries.possible_interpretation: unity, wholeness, need for closeness; (per Arabic handout) loneliness and need for support

entries.original_text: Flowers, sun, clouds: May be read as optimism, imagination, or positive mood when used in a dreamy context.
entries.possible_interpretation: optimism, imagination, or positive mood, when used in a dreamy context
entries.notes_as_written: No fixed rule; depends heavily on context.

entries.original_text: Hearts: Usually reflect affection, love, romance, or social warmth in a cultural sense.
entries.possible_interpretation: affection, love, romance, or social warmth
entries.notes_as_written: Symbolic meaning is culturally obvious, not psychometric.

entries.original_text: Transportation drawings: May suggest travel interest, movement, adventure, or a social/playful orientation.
entries.possible_interpretation: travel interest, movement, adventure, or a social/playful orientation

entries.original_text: House: Sometimes discussed as family life, safety, privacy, or emotional openness, but not a reliable standalone test.
entries.possible_interpretation: family life, safety, privacy, or emotional openness

entries.original_text: Tree: Sometimes used to think about stability, growth, roots, or vulnerability.
entries.possible_interpretation: stability, growth, roots, or vulnerability

entries.original_text: Repeated monsters, danger, injury themes: May indicate fear, distress, or preoccupation with threat; needs careful follow-up.
entries.possible_interpretation: fear, distress, or preoccupation with threat

entries.original_text: Very large drawing / fills the page: Sometimes linked with expansiveness, strong energy, or self-assertion; your handout links it to high self-esteem.
entries.possible_interpretation: expansiveness, strong energy, self-assertion; (per Arabic handout) high self-esteem
entries.notes_as_written: Page occupation is a common projective heuristic.

entries.original_text: Moderate drawing size (~half page): Sometimes read as balance or mixed approach; your handout says open at times and introverted at times.
entries.possible_interpretation: balance or mixed approach; (per Arabic handout) outgoing at times and introverted at times

entries.original_text: Very small drawing: May suggest insecurity, withdrawal, fear, or low confidence; could also reflect carefulness or skill limits.
entries.possible_interpretation: insecurity, withdrawal, fear, or low confidence
entries.notes_as_written: Size is a common but nonspecific cue.

entries.original_text: Uses only a small part of the page: May suggest caution, uncertainty, or low confidence.
entries.possible_interpretation: caution, uncertainty, or low confidence

entries.original_text: Top of page: Sometimes read as fantasy, dreaming, ambition, or being less grounded in current reality.
entries.possible_interpretation: fantasy, dreaming, ambition, or being less grounded in current reality

entries.original_text: Left side: Sometimes linked to introversion, past orientation, or dependence.
entries.possible_interpretation: introversion, past orientation, or dependence

entries.original_text: Right side: Sometimes linked to extroversion, future orientation, or outward movement.
entries.possible_interpretation: extroversion, future orientation, or outward movement

entries.original_text: Centering: Often read as balance, security, or comfort.
entries.possible_interpretation: balance, security, or comfort

entries.original_text: Heavy pressure: May suggest tension, force, anger, or high energy.
entries.possible_interpretation: tension, force, anger, or high energy
entries.notes_as_written: Not specific to emotion; can reflect motor style.

entries.original_text: Light pressure: May suggest hesitation, shyness, low energy, or delicacy.
entries.possible_interpretation: hesitation, shyness, low energy, or delicacy

entries.original_text: Shaky or broken lines: May suggest anxiety, uncertainty, distress, or motor difficulty.
entries.possible_interpretation: anxiety, uncertainty, distress, or motor difficulty
entries.notes_as_written: Needs comparison with age and motor skills.

entries.original_text: Zigzag lines: Sometimes read as agitation, violence, unpredictability, or conflict.
entries.possible_interpretation: agitation, violence, unpredictability, or conflict

entries.original_text: Over-erasing / frequent corrections: May suggest perfectionism, anxiety, frustration, or uncertainty.
entries.possible_interpretation: perfectionism, anxiety, frustration, or uncertainty

entries.original_text: Missing hands: Sometimes interpreted as difficulty acting, social difficulty, or avoidance.
entries.possible_interpretation: difficulty acting, social difficulty, or avoidance

entries.original_text: Missing mouth: Sometimes linked with difficulty expressing emotion or communication issues.
entries.possible_interpretation: difficulty expressing emotion or communication issues

entries.original_text: Missing eyes: May suggest avoidance or emotional withdrawal.
entries.possible_interpretation: avoidance or emotional withdrawal

entries.original_text: Exaggerated body parts: Huge hands, teeth, eyes, etc. may suggest aggression, fear, or hypervigilance.
entries.possible_interpretation: aggression, fear, or hypervigilance

entries.original_text: Repeated monsters or danger scenes: May reflect a recurring fear or preoccupation.
entries.possible_interpretation: a recurring fear or preoccupation

entries.original_text: Repeated family conflict scenes: May indicate tension, perceived conflict, or concern in the home.
entries.possible_interpretation: tension, perceived conflict, or concern in the home

entries.original_text: Repeated isolation themes: May point to loneliness or withdrawal.
entries.possible_interpretation: loneliness or withdrawal

entries.source_section: Mood or concern flags sometimes discussed
entries.original_text: Dark colors, sad faces, isolation: Sometimes flagged as possible sadness, low mood, or distress.
entries.possible_interpretation: possible sadness, low mood, or distress
entries.notes_as_written: Color evidence is mixed; not diagnostic.

entries.source_section: Mood or concern flags sometimes discussed
entries.original_text: Refusal to draw figures: May suggest distress, resistance, perfectionism, or lack of task engagement.
entries.possible_interpretation: distress, resistance, perfectionism, or lack of task engagement

entries.source_section: Mood or concern flags sometimes discussed
entries.original_text: Excessive detail or fixation: May suggest anxiety, obsession with parts of the task, or strong interest.
entries.possible_interpretation: anxiety, obsession with parts of the task, or strong interest

entries.source_section: Mood or concern flags sometimes discussed
entries.original_text: Neglect of background: May reflect focus on the main subject, limited time, or developmental style.
entries.possible_interpretation: focus on the main subject, limited time, or developmental style
entries.notes_as_written: Not a pathology sign by itself.

entries.original_text: Use these rules only as hypotheses. The most defensible reading comes from combining the drawing with the child's age, the drawing process, repeated patterns over time, and the child's own explanation. No single item here should be treated as proof of depression, abuse, anxiety, or personality type.

relationships.note: Same observable (wide eyes). Arabic source states 'outgoing personality' unconditionally; English source hedges with 'openness/alertness, or sometimes fear/surprise' -- broader and less certain.
Same observable (stern/narrowed eyes -> anger); English source broadens to include tension/suspicion/defensiveness.
Same observable and near-identical interpretation (closed eyes -> refusing to look inward / shutting out the world).
Same observable (tiger/wolf -> anger); English source adds threat/aggression.
Same observable (fox) but different specific interpretation: Arabic = malicious intent, English = sneakiness/cunning. Related valence, not identical claim.
Same observable and interpretation (squirrel -> need for protection); English adds nervous energy/seeking care.
Same observable and interpretation (lion -> superiority); English adds dominance/pride/strength.
Same observable (repeated geometric shapes -> stubbornness/persistence/goals/planning).
Same observable (stars -> wanting attention/admiration/visibility).

Same observable (flowers/sun/clouds -> optimism/positive mood). Arabic requires a strict behavioral precondition (drawn while distracted/absent-minded); English softens this to a vaguer 'dreamy context' -- the precondition is weakened, not identical.
Same observable; English source explicitly cites the Arabic handout's loneliness reading as part of its own broader interpretation (unity/wholeness/closeness).
Same observable and near-identical interpretation (vehicles -> travel/adventure/sociability).
Same observable and near-identical interpretation (hearts -> affection/love/social warmth).
Same observable; English source explicitly cites the Arabic handout's own wording ('open at times and introverted at times').
Same observable; English source explicitly cites the Arabic handout's 'high self-esteem' reading.
Same observable (page-area coverage, not absolute figure size) -- both frame the measure as a fraction of the page used, matching most directly.

English 'Very small drawing' conflates absolute figure smallness with the same fear/insecurity reading as the page-coverage rule; a genuinely distinct observable (figure size vs. page-area fraction) with an overlapping interpretation.

Internal to the English PDF: 'Very small drawing' and 'Uses only a small part of the page' describe closely related but not identical observables (figure size vs. page-area fraction) with overlapping interpretations (insecurity/withdrawal/fear/low confidence vs. caution/uncertainty/low confidence).
Same observable and near-identical interpretation (top placement -> dreaminess/fantasy/difficulty adapting).
Same observable (left placement -> introversion); English adds past orientation/dependence.
Same observable (right placement -> extraversion); English adds future orientation/outward movement.

Internal to the English PDF: 'Repeated monsters, danger, injury themes' (page 2, Animals and objects with stories) and 'Repeated monsters or danger scenes' (page 3, Repeated themes) describe the same observable with near-identical wording -- the PDF itself restates this row across two sections.

Internal to the English PDF: 'Eyes with little detail or missing eyes' (page 1, Eyes and face) and 'Missing eyes' (page 3, Missing or altered details) describe overlapping observables (absence/low-detail of eyes) with overlapping interpretations (withdrawal/avoidance).

Both concern loneliness, but the observable differs entirely: Arabic/EN_013 is a shape-based proxy (drawing circles); EN_039 is a content/scene-based theme (repeated isolation scenes) -- not the same measurable observable, so related, not duplicate.
New observable (general facial expression / smiling vs. sad/tense/frightened) not present in the Arabic source at all -- expands the 'eyes and face' evidence family.
New observable (animal choice in general, independent of species) not present in the Arabic source.
New observables (house, tree) with no Arabic counterpart.
New observable (centering) with no Arabic counterpart.
An entirely new evidence family (line quality/pressure appearance) with no Arabic counterpart at all.
New observables (missing hands, missing mouth, exaggerated body parts) with no Arabic counterpart.

New observables (repeated family conflict, dark-colour/sad-face/isolation combination, refusal to draw figures, excessive detail, background neglect) with no Arabic counterpart -- these are the PDF's own 'mood or concern flags', all self-labeled 'Suggestive only' or weaker.
